references.text: In Mark's parallel account, the blind Bartimaeus hears that it is Jesus of Nazareth passing by and begins to call out to him. Both texts describe the blind man hearing the crowd pass and seeking to understand what is happening ([ref:Mark 10:46-47|Mark 10:46-47]).
Matthew's parallel account of the healing of the blind near Jericho, where the blind also perceive that Jesus is passing by and cry out to him ([ref:Matt 20:29-30|Matt 20:29-30]).
The following verse in which the crowd answers the blind man that it is Jesus of Nazareth passing by—the answer to the question he asked in verse 36 ([ref:Luk 18:37|Luke 18:37]).

Zacchaeus also wants to see who Jesus is as he passes through Jericho and takes action to find out—a similar situation where someone seeks to understand what is happening while Jesus travels through the city ([ref:Luk 19:3-4|Luke 19:3-4]).
Another situation in which a crowd (ὄχλος) presses around Jesus, creating confusion and obstacles for those seeking him ([ref:Luk 8:42|Luke 8:42]).
